notes: The supplied target is Relationship between flexibility (new product introduction) and discipline (waste) in the overall sample. These are Collins et al. (1998) factors discussed as the prior study, not the named regression outcomes/predictors in the present study. Table 7 instead tests DISCIPLINE against CUSTOM, VOLFLEX, MIXFLEX and TTM, in separate Step 2 direct-effect and Step 3 moderated models. Table 4 compares item sets; it does not establish corresponding regression tests by vertical row position. No explicit mapping identifies a unique target. No assignment by order, numerical match, or assumed equivalence was made. Table 7 candidate standardized-variable coefficients, each [Step 2, Step 3]: CUSTOM [.135 (p < .05), .363 (p < .001)]; VOLFLEX [.236 (p < .001), .486 (p < .001)]; MIXFLEX [.267 (p < .001), .360 (p < .001)]; TTM [.106 (no significance marker), .237 (p < .05)]. Candidate model analytic N is explicitly printed as 285 in the table title; retained only for parent field-scope review because row correspondence is unresolved. No calculation performed. All variables are explicitly standardized (Table footnote a); no metric conversion performed. The conclusion provides an overall favorable verdict on the rigid flexibility model, but no verdict on the specifically supplied factor pair. Rendered PDF pages 7 and 9 were inspected. Original side is an unassigned placeholder.
